variants.headline: Business-start grant programme ends
variants.sub: Business-starting support under {programme} has come to an end.
variants.body:
The programme {programme} has ended, having paid {paid} grants and refused {refused} applications. It supported people starting a business. Readers considering {target} should distinguish that record from a judgment that either the existence or the end of a programme proves it served its purpose adequately.

Our principles require public support to be judged by the purpose it is meant to serve. We hold {target} responsible for inadequate political judgment and insist upon a more demanding public standard.

variants.headline: A grant scheme closes its account
variants.sub: The programme {programme} has ended its support for people starting a business.
variants.body:
A grant programme's record contains refusals as well as payments. The programme {programme} has ended with {paid} grants paid and {refused} applications refused. For {target}, the question is how to judge support for people starting a business through that full record, rather than the attraction of the scheme's title.

Our principles require public support to be judged by the purpose it is meant to serve. We hold {target} responsible for inadequate political judgment and insist upon a more demanding public standard.

variants.headline: Support programme reaches its end
variants.sub: The grant programme {programme} for people starting a business has ended.
variants.body:
Support under {programme} has come to an end. The programme paid {paid} grants and refused {refused} applications from people seeking to start a business. An assessment of {target} should consider what responsible public support means, without assuming a particular reason for the programme's conclusion.

Our principles require public support to be judged by the purpose it is meant to serve. We hold {target} responsible for inadequate political judgment and insist upon a more demanding public standard.
